answer: My anti-Sybil design is a hilltop signal relay. Each verifier tends one station anchored by a relic stone and a yarrow patch. Twice daily it flashes a coded signal by mirror, and neighbours log the flash time and the yarrow's growth, which no script can fake from afar. A new identity needs vouching from two adjacent stations that watched its signal for a full moon cycle; a station reporting a flash nobody else saw loses its stone and restarts. Since the yarrow, the stone and the sky must agree, one operator cannot run many stations cheaply: each needs real ground, plants and neighbours.
